new_candidates.body:
Thanks for releasing FineART. While running some acceptance checks on the first two data files (`data/chunk-000/file-000.parquet` and `file-001.parquet`, revision `135d9b0`, 501 episodes), I found that `observation.state` at frame t equals `action` at frame t-1 exactly, on all 14 dims, in every frame I checked (141,928 frames in the first 40 episodes, max absolute difference 0.0).

So one of the two streams isn't independently measured: either the action was derived from the next recorded state (`action[t] = state[t+1]`), or the state was filled in from the previous command. The card describes state as "joint + gripper positions" and action as "joint + gripper targets", so it would help users to know which it is:

- If actions are next-state, they carry no tracking error, and gripper commands that squeeze past the blocked position during a grasp won't appear in the data.
- If state is the previous command, a policy conditioned on state sees the action it's asked to predict, one frame late, and never sees where the arm actually was.

To reproduce:

```python
import numpy as np, pyarrow.parquet as pq

t = pq.read_table("data/chunk-000/file-000.parquet",
                  columns=["episode_index", "frame_index", "observation.state", "action"])
ep, fi = np.asarray(t["episode_index"]), np.asarray(t["frame_index"])
state = np.asarray(t["observation.state"].to_pylist())
action = np.asarray(t["action"].to_pylist())
for e in np.unique(ep)[:5]:
    i = np.where(ep == e)[0]
    i = i[np.argsort(fi[i])]
    print(e, np.abs(state[i][1:] - action[i][:-1]).max())  # 0.0 for every episode
```

Happy to run the same check over the full set if that's useful.
new_candidates.title: FineART: observation.state[t] equals action[t-1] exactly in every frame

new_candidates.body:
### Describe the bug

With `--renderer ovrtx`, Isaac Lab 3.0.0 cannot load a scene that holds a large Gaussian splat. OVRTX fails while it opens the scene:

```
OvstageError: OP_FAILED: failed to parse inline USDA into anonymous layer
```

Isaac Lab passes the scene to OVRTX as USDA text. `export_stage_to_string` flattens the stage and returns `ExportToString()`, and the renderer passes that string to `open_usd_from_string`. The text is broken before OVRTX sees it. OpenUSD's USDA writer replaces any attribute value whose text is longer than 2^31 - 1 characters with at most 4,095 bytes, and it reports no error. We reported that limit to OpenUSD in https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD/issues/4323. The cause is `ArchVStringPrintf`, which gets -1 from `vsnprintf` for output longer than `INT_MAX`.

Our scene is a 3DGS capture. It has one `ParticleField3DGaussianSplat` with 8,000,000 splats and degree-3 spherical harmonics, so its `radiance:sphericalHarmonicsCoefficients` holds 128,000,000 float3 values, which print as about 5.26 billion characters of text. On 3.0.0 the export took 53.6 s, and OVRTX 0.5.1 rejected the text after another 11.6 s. When OVRTX 0.5.1 opens the same file itself, it shows the first image after 3.9 s and then takes 8.7 ms per 640x480 frame.

On `main` (6bb6548), the bug is narrower. #8769 (merged 2026-10-23, after v3.0.0, not on `release/3.0.0`) keeps clean file-backed references in the export, so a splat referenced from a saved file stays out of the text. Our scene exports as 454 characters. From the code, the exporter still bakes the full data in these cases:

- The splat is authored in the stage's own layers: root, session, or sublayers. We ran this case.
- A referenced layer is anonymous or has unsaved edits (`isaaclab_ov/stage.py:314` and `:326-327`).
- The renderer shares an OVStage with physics, which sets `preserve_references=False` (`renderers/ovrtx_renderer.py:389-391`).
- `OvPhysxManager` exports a shared scene with the default `preserve_references=False` (`physics/ovphysx_manager.py:727-733`).

### Steps to reproduce

The script needs only `pxr` and `numpy`, and it peaks at about 5 GB of memory. It writes 53,000,000 float3 values. Each value prints as `(-0.12345679, -0.12345679, -0.12345679)`, so the array text is 2,173,000,000 characters, just over 2^31 - 1. The whole layer would be 2,173,000,217 characters.

```python
import numpy as np
from pxr import Sdf, Usd, Vt

stage = Usd.Stage.CreateInMemory()
stage.DefinePrim("/World", "Xform")
prim = stage.DefinePrim("/World/Splat", "ParticleField3DGaussianSplat")
values = Vt.Vec3fArray.FromNumpy(np.full((53_000_000, 3), -0.12345679, np.float32))
prim.CreateAttribute("radiance:sphericalHarmonicsCoefficients", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float3Array).Set(values)

usda = stage.ExportToString()
print(len(usda))
Sdf.Layer.CreateAnonymous(".usda").ImportFromString(usda)
```

The script prints 4309 instead of 2173000217. `ImportFromString` then raises a parse error: `Expected } at 'float3[] radiance:sphericalHarmonicsCoefficients ='`.

This is the string Isaac Lab hands to OVRTX:

- On v3.0.0, `export_stage_to_string(stage, 1, source_paths=())` returns `stage.ExportToString()` for one environment (`isaaclab_ov/renderers/ovrtx_usd.py:426`). The renderer passes it to OVRTX at `ovrtx_renderer.py:506` and `:604`.
- On `main`, `export_stage_to_string` ends with `layer.ExportToString()` (`isaaclab_ov/stage.py:351`). We ran that function, copied from `main`, on the stage from the script with 110,000,000 values and `preserve_references=True`. It returned 4,527 characters instead of about 4,510,000,000. The renderer passes the string to `OvstageBackend.populate` (`ovrtx_renderer.py:409`, then `stage.py:195`) or to `renderer.open_usd_from_string` (`ovrtx_renderer.py:411`).

With OVRTX 0.5.1, `ovstage.population.open_usd_from_string` fails on such a string with the error above.

### System Info

- Commit: v3.0.0 (e3f7d9f) for the runs. We read the code on `main` at 6bb6548.
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.2.0 (pip packages), with OVRTX 0.5.1, OVStage 0.2.1, and the bundled OpenUSD 26.08. OpenUSD 26.11 (`usd-core` from PyPI) gives the same result.
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition
- CUDA: 13.0
- GPU Driver: 580.159.04

### Additional context

A `.usda` file has the same limit, because `Sdf.Layer.Export` uses the same writer. The layer from the script exports to a 4,243-byte `.usda` file. A `.usdc` file has no such limit, and the same layer round-trips through `.usdc` with all 53,000,000 values.

Draft PR #8764 already moves the OVStage hand-off to a temporary `.usdc` file, to cut startup time. It would also fix this bug on the OVStage path. The legacy path through `renderer.open_usd_from_string` would still need the same change.

Suggested fix:

1. Whenever the exporter bakes the stage, pass OVRTX and OVStage a `.usdc` file, as #8764 does, on both paths.
2. Backport #8769 to `release/3.0.0`, so a splat referenced from a saved file works in 3.0.x.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)
- [x] I have checked that the issue is not in running Isaac Sim itself and is related to the repo

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `--renderer ovrtx`, a scene with one attribute over 2^31 - 1 characters of USDA text, such as an 8,000,000-splat degree-3 `ParticleField3DGaussianSplat`, loads on both the OVStage and the legacy path.
- [ ] Until then, the renderer fails with an error that names the attribute, not with OVRTX's parse error.
- [ ] #8769 ships in a 3.0.x release.
new_candidates.title: [Bug Report] OVRTX renderer cannot load a scene with a large Gaussian splat because the USDA hand-off cuts values longer than 2^31 - 1 characters
